title: Lecture 2 — signed numbers, overflow, and logic gates
summary: Signed binary encodings let a fixed-width register represent positive and negative integers. Two's-complement arithmetic makes addition and subtraction share the same circuitry, while overflow and extension rules explain what happens at the limits.
body: Start by comparing sign-magnitude with two's complement. In two's complement, negation means inverting the bits and adding one, so subtraction can be performed as addition. Because an $N$-bit register keeps only $N$ result bits, the mathematical sum may wrap outside the signed range; overflow detection identifies that case. Sign extension preserves a negative value when the register widens, and the final logic-gate tables connect these bit operations to their circuit-level building blocks.
